The screen goes dark for about a minute while it starts back up. Music, calls and CarPlay stop until then.

Android won’t let one app close another, so a small helper does the tapping: for Restart it presses Force stop on %1$s and opens it again, and for Reboot it uses the power menu. It also runs auto-fix and the floating button. It only looks at the screen to find those buttons and to see whether CarPlay is showing, and it never saves or sends anything.
Find CarPlay Restart (it can be under Downloaded apps or Installed services) and turn it on.
Says Restricted setting? Go to Settings › Apps › CarPlay Restart, tap ⋮ at the top, choose Allow restricted settings, then try again.

Lets CarPlay Restart close and reopen your CarPlay app. When you press Restart (in the app, on the floating button or on the widget), it opens the app’s App info page, presses Force stop (clearing the app’s cache first if you asked), then opens the app again and, if you picked one in Settings, presses its Apple CarPlay or Android Auto button. When you hold Reboot radio, it opens the power menu and presses Restart. If auto-fix is on, it checks every few seconds whether your CarPlay app is showing CarPlay, and restarts the app when CarPlay doesn’t come back. It doesn’t save or send anything it sees.
